meta.title_plain: How Federer went from racket-thrower to legend
meta.teaser: He won only 54% of his points. Here's why that made him a champion.

page.title: How Federer went from racket‑thrower to legend
page.sub: The Founders podcast on Roger Federer's secrets
page.bigIdea: Federer won only 54% of the points he played. Champions don't win every point. They let the bad ones go.

cards.title: He used to lose his temper
cards.front: As a kid, Federer threw rackets and yelled on court.
cards.back: An opponent said Roger would fall apart after two hours. That stung. At 16, he started training his mind.
cards.tryit: After a bad point, take one deep breath before the next one.

cards.title: Control the flames
cards.front: He didn't lose his fire. He learned to aim it.
cards.back: Federer turned his anger into energy. Same fire, pointed in a better direction.
cards.tryit: When you get mad in a match, pour it into your next serve.

cards.title: It's only a point
cards.front: He won just over half the points he played.
cards.back: Even the greatest lose almost half the points. So he forgot bad points fast and played the next one fully.
cards.tryit: After a mistake, say in your head: 'It's only a point.'

cards.title: Rest is part of training
cards.front: His trainer planned for a very long career.
cards.back: Their rule: stress, recover, improve. Hard work plus real rest kept him playing as a pro for 24 years.
cards.tryit: Take one real rest day after your next tough tournament.

cards.title: Never stop loving it
cards.front: Federer said he never fell out of love with tennis.
cards.back: He kept tennis fun by changing his routines, so it never got boring.
cards.tryit: Try one new shot or drill this week just for fun.

words.d: Losing control when you're upset or angry.
Staying calm and in control under pressure.
Rest your body and mind need to get stronger after hard work.
A coach who trains how you think and feel when you compete.

quiz.q: What percentage of points did Federer win in his career?
quiz.hint: It's a lot lower than you'd guess!
quiz.why: Just over half. Even the best lose lots of points, so letting them go matters.

quiz.q: What was Federer like on court as a kid?
quiz.why: He had a big temper and had to learn to control it.

quiz.hint: Getting stronger needs two things, not just one.
quiz.why: Hard work only pays off when you also recover.

quiz.q: What did Federer do with his anger?
opts: Turned it into energy and focus
quiz.why: He kept his fire but learned to aim it.

page.think: What happens in your head after you lose a point? What could you do in the 20 seconds before the next one?
